{{Quote|I shall reassert our position of neutrality.''"<br />"''The talk of an ''idealist''.''"<br />"''No, those are the words of a ''pacifist'', and a people who have chosen nonviolent action.|[[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]] and [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] [[Vice Chair/Legends|Vice Chair]] [[Mas Amedda/Legends|Mas Amedda]], arguing the political stance of the New Mandalorians|<ref name="TCW:DoM" />}}
The '''New Mandalorians''' were members of a reformist [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Politics/Legends|political]] movement on [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. The group was formed after a [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Mandalorian Excision|attack]] on the [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalore sector]] which rendered portions of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] into inhospitable [[Color/Legends|white]]-sand [[Desert/Legends|deserts]]. Differing from other groups on Mandalore in that they placed great importance on virtues of pacifism, neutrality, and nonviolence, rather than military strength, the New Mandalorians used their [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]]' technical skill and their talent for construction to forge a new society in the barren wastes. There, segregated from the warrior clans of the rest of Mandalore's people, the New Mandalorians lived in grand [[Bio-cube/Legends|bio-cube]] [[City/Legends|cities]], taking the [[Domed city/Legends|domed city]] of [[Sundari/Legends|Sundari]] to be their [[Capital/Legends|capital]]. The New Mandalorians disregarded the ancient Mandalorian [[Canons of Honor|warrior codes]], and forwent traditional [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]], as they turned their backs on their warrior clan peers and diverged from the ''[[Resol'nare]]'', the central tenets of Mandalorian culture. A number of Mandalorian hardliners in [[Aka'liit|support]] of the traditional warrior culture subsequently deemed the New Mandalorians as the '''Faithless''' due to the perceived illegitimacy of their peaceful counterculture.

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the New Mandalorians were led by [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]] of [[Kalevala/Legends|Kalevala]], and their [[Ruling Council (New Mandalorians)/Legends|government]] combated the rival Mandalorian movement known as the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]], in an [[Mandalore Defense Resolution/Legends|effort]] to keep Mandalore neutral, and out of the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] war. Neutrality came at a cost, however, leading to severe [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] shortages, and a [[Mandalorian black market conspiracy/Legends|rise]] in New Mandalorian corruption as the Republic severed [[Hyperspace route/Legends|trade routes]] to Mandalore, leaving the desert-dwelling New Mandalorians scrambling to feed their people, cut off as they were from Mandalore's verdant [[Farm/Legends|farming]] communities. Late in the war, the New Mandalorian regime [[Takeover of Mandalore/Legends|fell]] to the [[Shadow Collective/Legends|machinations]] of a Death Watch coup that saw Duchess Kryze deposed, and the radicals' rise to power behind the puppet [[Prime Minister/Legends|Prime Minister]] [[Almec/Legends|Almec]]. These revanchists heralded the demise of the New Mandalorians and their ideals, and their political dominance on Mandalore came to an end following the ascendance of [[Spar]] to the position of [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']], traditional leader of the Mandalorian people.

==Description==
===Society and government===
{{Quote|Your peaceful ways have paid off. Mandalore has prospered since the last time I was here.''"<br />"''Not everyone on Mandalore believes that our commitment to peace is a sign of progress.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and Satine Kryze|<ref name="TCW:TMP" />}}
[[File:PeacePark-TMP.png|thumb|left|300px|The tranquil [[Peace Park/Legends|Peace Park]], designed, built, and frequented by the pacifistic New Mandalorians]]
The New Mandalorians were a reformist [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] faction. Unlike the Mandalorians' traditional history as [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]], the New Mandalorians fashioned themselves as pacifists, espousing the virtues of peace, tolerance, and neutrality. They came to view these ideals as necessities to surviving in a hostile [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], and did away with the ancient [[Canons of Honor|warrior codes]] their forebearers had followed in the hope of being accepted by the [[galactic community]].<ref name="TEA" /> Instead of training in combat, the New Mandalorians cultivated their talents as inventors and pursued their passion for advanced technology.<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> Non-violence was an expectation for all within their sect,<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> but while violent [[Blood/Legends|bloodshed]] toward [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] was abhorrent to the New Mandalorians,<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> non-[[Death/Legends|lethal]] self-defense was acceptable in certain situations.<ref name="TCW:VoT" /> The New Mandalorians looked down upon their warrior clan brethren for continuing their age-old ways as soldiers and [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], believing that their traditions were discredited and that they were ultimately dead-enders.<ref name="TEA" />

Following their foundation, the New Mandalorians established a society of their own, isolated from the traditional Mandalorian warrior clans on their cultural [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]].<ref name="TEA" /> They took to the portions of Mandalore that had been rendered into barren [[Desert/Legends|deserts]] of [[Color/Legends|white]] sand<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] devastating [[Mandalorian Excision]],<ref name="TEGW" /> constructing massive [[Bio-cube/Legends|bio-cube]] [[City/Legends|cities]]<ref name="Mandalore">{{SWE|locations|mandalore|Mandalore}}</ref> using their innovative technological skills.<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> Hermetically sealed against the elements,<ref name="Gauntlet">{{SWE|technology|gauntlet-fighter|Gauntlet fighter}}</ref> these bio-cube cities allowed the New Mandalorians to live within Mandalore's inhospitable deserts,<ref name="Mandalore" /> and the grand black-[[Domed city/Legends|domed city]] of [[Sundari/Legends|Sundari]] was taken as the New Mandalorians' [[Capital/Legends|capital]].<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> Many of the New Mandalorians' vehicles were purchased from the [[MandalMotors/Legends|MandalMotors]] company,<ref name="TCWIV">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]''</ref> a driving force in Mandalore's economy<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> that was headquartered in the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] traditional capital city of [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]].<ref name="HotM">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref> MandalMotors-made [[Aka'jor-class shuttle/Legends|''Aka'jor''-class shuttles]], [[Buirk'alor-class airspeeder|''Buirk'alor''-class airspeeders]], and [[Balutar-class swoop/Legends|''Balutar''-class swoops]] could all be found employed throughout New Mandalorian society.<ref name="TCWIV" /> Despite coming from a company owned and operated by the Mandalorian warrior clans,<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> in keeping with their pacifist ideals, these New Mandalorian vessels were all unarmed.<ref name="TCWIV" /> In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> it was declared illegal for offworlders to carry weapons<ref name="TCW:TA">{{TCW|The Academy}}</ref> in New Mandalorian territories.<ref name="NewBattlefronts" />

[[File:New_Mandalorian_ministry_council.png|thumb|right|275px|The New Mandalorian Ruling Council]]
Unlike the warrior clans, who were governed by a loose organization of the many [[Chief/Legends|chieftains]] of the clans subordinate to the reigning [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']]<ref name="ImpCom501st">''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''</ref>—the traditional leader of the Mandalorian people and culture<ref name="TMPaC">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref>—the New Mandalorian government was more centralized, comprised of a [[Ruling Council (New Mandalorians)/Legends|Ruling Council]]<ref name="Corruption" /> made up of a number of ministers, such as the [[Minister of Finance (New Mandalorians)/Legends|Minister of Finance]] and the [[Minister of the Interior/Legends|Minister of the Interior]].<ref name="CorruptionEpGuide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode305.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Corruption}}</ref> The council was presided over by a [[Prime Minister/Legends|Prime Minister]]<ref name="Corruption" /> and a [[Deputy Minister/Legends|Deputy Minister]],<ref name="TCW:DoM" /> and operated out of the [[Sundari Royal Palace/Legends|Sundari Royal Palace]].<ref name="Corruption" /> The New Mandalorians did not recognize the authority of the clan-chosen ''Mand'alor'',<ref name="TEGW" /> instead appointing a ''Mand'alor'' of their own in opposition to the leader of the warrior clans. To the traditional warriors who resented the New Mandalorians, these leaders were known as "[[Anti-Mandalore]]s."<ref name="TBHC">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref> Establishing a peaceful and stable state they deemed "New Mandalore,"<ref name="UKComic6.20">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.20|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Comic 6.20]]</ref> the New Mandalorians were the first Mandalorian group to gain the acceptance of the Republic,<ref name="TCSWE" /> culminating in Mandalore being granted [[Senator/Legends|representation]] in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]].<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> The New Mandalorian government made all attempts to ensure the sect remained neutral and removed from any conflict that sought to involve them,<ref name="TCW:DoM" /> though the Ruling Council's many ministers were prone to squabbling amongst themselves over decisions regarding the New Mandalorian people, and over [[Time/Legends|time]], corruption of the government's officials became a growing concern.<ref name="Corruption" />

===People and culture===
{{Quote|Our people were warriors. Strong. ''Feared!'' Now they're ruled by the New Mandalorians who think that being a ''pacifist'' is a ''good'' thing. They've given away our honor and tradition for ''peace''. Duchess Satine and her corrupt leadership are crushing our souls, ''destroying'' our identity!|[[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]]|<ref name="Eminence">{{TCW|Eminence (episode)}}</ref>}}
[[File:NewMandalorianPeople.png|thumb|left|325px|A vast crowd of New Mandalorian citizens]]
The New Mandalorian populous was overwhelmingly composed of [[Human/Legends|Humans]], with fair-complected skin, and primarily blonde [[Hair/Legends|hair]],<ref name="TCW:TMP" /><ref name="Corruption" /><ref name="SoR">{{TCW|Shades of Reason}}</ref> though individuals with brown<ref name="Corruption" /> and red hair were known to exist within the New Mandalorian faction.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> This racial homogeneity stood in stark contrast to the traditional warrior clans,<ref name="TMPaC" /> in which Humans of a variety of skin colors<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref> and [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] from a multitude of [[Species/Legends|species]] all stood together as Mandalorians,<ref name="TEGW" /> regardless of outward appearances. Further separating them from the warrior clans,<ref name="TMPaC" /> the New Mandalorian civilian population forwent traditional [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]] as part of their proscription of violence,<ref name="TEA" /> a significant deviation from the ''[[Resol'nare]]'', the six central tenets of the Mandalorian culture that traditionally defined what it meant to be Mandalorian.<ref name="TMPaC" /> Instead, the average New Mandalorian citizen primarily dressed in more casual [[Clothing/Legends|attire]], such as pants, [[shirt]]s, tunics, and dresses.<ref name="SoR" /> Even without armor, a number of New Mandalorians continued to wear<ref name="Corruption" /> traditional Mandalorian [[Kama/Legends|''kamas'']].<ref name="GttGAR">{{InsiderCite|84|Guide to the Grand Army of the Republic}}</ref> New Mandalorian garments were often white in color, though shades of blue<ref name="SoR" />—a color that had long represented the concept of reliability in the Mandalorian culture<ref name="Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref>—were also common in New Mandalorian fashion.<ref name="SoR" />

Officers of the New [[Mandalorian Guard/Legends|Mandalorian police]] force were among the few who continued to wear [[Armor/Legends|armor]] in the course of their duties, utilizing uniform suits of grey-plated armor<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> that shared a number of design elements in common with the style of armor worn by traditional Mandalorian soldiers of the time.<ref name="TBHC" /> The [[Mandalorian Royal Guard/Legends|Mandalorian Royal Guard]] also wore suits of armor, specifically designed to evoke Mandalore's history of gallantry and discipline, while at the same time setting itself apart from the armor associated with Mandalore's warrior clans.<ref name="TCWCE">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

After breaking from the Mandalorian warrior clans,<ref name="TEA" /> the New Mandalorians retained the knowledge of how to work Mandalorian [[Beskar/Legends|''beskar'']] [[Iron/Legends|iron]],<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> a nearly indestructible<ref name="HotM" /> metal [[Ore/Legends|ore]] found only on Mandalore<ref name="Sacrifice" /> and its [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]].<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> The Mandalorians historically developed techniques for manipulating the iron which they guarded closely from outsiders, and passed down from one generation to the next;<ref name="HotM" /> the New Mandalorians used ''beskar'' in the construction of their capital, Sundari, and in the city's towering buildings.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" />

[[File:Mandalorian_pupils.jpg|thumb|right|300px|New Mandalorian students eating a [[Sundari Mandalorian school/Legends|school]] meal]]
New Mandalorian culture was very clinical, and tightly [[Regiment/Legends|regimented]],<ref name="CMF">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Two]] ("Creating Mandalore" featurette)</ref> with elements of their warrior heritage redirected toward other pursuits or kept firmly throttled by the domineering government.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> While they dwelt in the white-sand desert regions of Mandalore,<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> the New Mandalorians still held an appreciation for natural greenery, though they insisted upon meticulously trimming and sculpting the vegetation into stark geometric shapes, everything from plaza-occupying [[Tree/Legends|trees]] to rooftop [[Garden/Legends|garden]] [[Bush/Legends|shrubs]].<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> New Mandalorian aesthetics often favored a cube shape,<ref name="CorruptionEpGuide" /> and such forms could be seen in numerous aspects of their daily lives, from the design of their bio-cube cities,<ref name="Mandalore" /> to the trim of Sundari's trees,<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> and even the cut of New Mandalorian [[Foodstuff/Legends|foods]].<ref name="CorruptionEpGuide" /> Such cube-cut food was served at the Sundari Royal Palace, and as part of the standardized meals served to New Mandalorian [[Youngling/Legends|children]] at their schools, along with fresh drinking [[Water/Legends|water]]. The New Mandalorians preferred centralized education for their children,<ref name="Corruption" /> as opposed to the warrior clans' individualistic education from their elders.<ref name="TMPaC" /> The most promising New Mandalorian students were enrolled in the prestigious [[Royal Academy of Government/Legends|Royal Academy of Government]], where they were taught and trained in the expectation that they would go on to be future leaders in the New Mandalorian government.<ref name="TCW:TA" />

==History==
===Formation===
{{Quote|Mandalore's violent past is behind us.|[[Almec/Legends|Almec]], [[Prime Minister/Legends|Prime Minister]] of the New Mandalorians|<ref name="TCW:TMP" />}}
In the year [[1051 BBY]], the Mandalorian soldier [[Mandalore the Uniter|Aga Awaud]] became the new ''Mand'alor'', taking the title of "Mandalore the Uniter" as he moved to [[Return (Mandalorian)|consolidate]] the Mandalorians scattered throughout the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] in an effort to strengthen Mandalorian [[Realspace/Legends|space]] following the ravages of the [[New Sith Wars]]. Under his reign, the [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalore sector]] emerged a regional industrial power, offering protection to surrounding [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] and [[Sector/Legends|sectors]] that lacked Mandalore's stability. To the Galactic Republic, however—piecing itself back together after the war with the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]—the Mandalorians were seen as a threat: taxing trade on the nearby [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]], binding their neighbors with defense and economic pacts, and refusing to comply with the Republic's [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|restrictions]] on sector defense forces. Though a number of clan leaders warned against<ref name="TEGW" /> Mandalore's growing militancy,<ref name="TEA" /> and argued that Mandalore should join the Republic as a powerful and influential sector, these would-be peacemakers were dismissed.<ref name="TEGW" />

[[File:Sundari_Desert.png|thumb|left|320px|In one of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore's]] post-[[Mandalorian Excision|Excision]] desert regions sat [[Sundari/Legends|Sundari]], the domed capital city of the New Mandalorian faction.]]
Alarmed by the threat of the Mandalorians, the Republic and its [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] protectors<ref name="TEA" /> lead a task force into Mandalorian space in [[738 BBY]], in a brief but overwhelming pre-emptive strike that came to be known as the Mandalorian Excision. Key Mandalorian worlds such as [[Ordo/Legends|Ordo]], [[Fenel]], [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]], and even Mandalore itself were bombarded by Republic forces to such a degree<ref name="TEGW" /> that portions of those worlds were transformed into barren desert.<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> Mandalorian space was disarmed and occupied for [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]], and a caretaker government was placed in power, comprised of those clan leaders who had sought peace. Over time, a new faction emerged from the caretaker government, calling themselves the "New Mandalorians": though they resented the Republic for its actions, the New Mandalorians saw no future in opposing the galactic government and chose instead to turn away from their warrior heritage,<ref name="TEGW" /> relinquishing their ancient warrior codes and traditional armor in exchange for a pacifistic creed espousing peace, neutrality, and tolerance. They chose to found a new society on Mandalore, isolated from the planet's warrior clans<ref name="TEA" /> in the white-sand deserts<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> left by the Mandalorian Excision,<ref name="TEGW" /> calling upon their talents as inventors and builders to forge grand<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> bio-cube cities in the inhospitable wastes.<ref name="Mandalore" /> The New Mandalorians took the domed city of Sundari as their capital,<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> in opposition to the traditional Mandalorian capital city of Keldabe,<ref name="TEA" /> and their dedication to peace and their love of advanced technology<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> allowed for them to claim ascendancy over the scattered warrior clans on Mandalore for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]].<ref name="TEA" /> For the first time in the planet's history<ref name="TCSWE" /> Mandalore was welcomed by the Republic, and offered representation in the Galactic Senate.<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> The New Mandalorians held most positions of power recognized by the Republic,<ref name="TEGW" /> and looked down upon the Mandalorian clans that still continued their warrior ways.<ref name="TEA" /> These practitioners of the traditional ways came to be known as the ''[[Aka'liit]]''—the Mandalorian Faithful—and, in turn, deemed the New Mandalorians the Faithless, with many viewing their alternate society as illegitimate.<ref name="TBHC" /> As time passed, the New Mandalorians eventually established a presence on Mandalore's neighboring world, [[Kalevala/Legends|Kalevala]].<ref name="TCW:DoM" />

===Civil wars===
{{Quote|The mercenary Jaster Mereel, who became Mandalore in 60 BBY, sought to reinstitute the warrior codes. His True Mandalorians were opposed by mercenaries who argued that the way to restore the clans' honor was to topple the hated New Mandalorians and repay the Republic's savagery in kind. This group became known as the Death Watch.|[[Vilnau Teupt]]|<ref name="TEGW" />}}
[[File:JasterMereelBlaster.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']] [[Jaster Mereel]], a fighter for [[Supercommando Codex|reform]] among the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] clans]]
Though many Mandalorian warriors were ambivalent toward the pacifist New Mandalorians,<ref name="TEGW" /> over the centuries, radical elements worked in secret to bring down their regime.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> In the year [[60 BBY/Legends|60 BBY]],<ref name="TEGW" /> a charismatic Mandalorian soldier by the name of [[Jaster Mereel]] ascended to the position of ''Mand'alor''. In this role, he began to institute a cultural reform among the clans that were unaffiliated with the New Mandalorians, a reform that many had been calling for since the [[Ithullan]] [[Mandalorian–Ithullan war|genocide]] nearly a [[200 BBY/Legends|century and a half]] earlier. Eventually laying out a new guideline for Mandalorian behavior known as the [[Supercommando Codex]],<ref name="HotM" /> he asserted that the Mandalorians who still wished to fight would simply act as highly-paid soldiers, and should conduct themselves as honorable mercenaries. Mereel was opposed by the barbaric<ref name="OpenSeasons">''[[Star Wars: Jango Fett: Open Seasons]]''</ref> [[Tor Vizsla]]<ref name="TEA" /> and his faction calling itself the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]], a group that desired a return to brutal savagery, the instigation of another galactic [[Mandalorian Wars|war of conquest]],<ref name="OpenSeasons" /> and the downfall of the New Mandalorians,<ref name="TEGW" /> whom they despised for their pacifist ideals and turning their back on the Mandalorians' traditional culture. While Death Watch's goals were quite opposite to the New Mandalorians,<ref name="Eminence" /> the New Mandalorians could not support Mereel's faction<ref name="TEA" /> of [[Mandalorian Supercommando|supercommandos]]—now calling themselves the "[[True Mandalorians]]"—for despite his reforms,<ref name="HotM" /> ''any'' act of Mandalorian violence was fundamentally against what the New Mandalorians stood for.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" />

The Death Watch and their True Mandalorian foes became embroiled in a bitter conflict dubbed the [[Mandalorian Civil War (True Mandalorians)|Mandalorian Civil War]];<ref name="HotM" /> the New Mandalorian government, meanwhile, rejected both groups and continued to act independently from them.<ref name="TEA" /> The war spanned more than a decade, during which Jaster Mereel fell and [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] took his place as the new ''Mand'alor'', up until the disastrous [[Battle of Galidraan]]<ref name="OpenSeasons" /> in [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]]<ref name="TEGW" /> that saw the eradication of the True Mandalorians from which Fett emerged as the only survivor. Though he hunted and killed Tor Vizsla on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]],<ref name="OpenSeasons" /> fragmenting and scattering the Death Watch,<ref name="HotM" /> Fett grew distant from his role as ''Mand'alor'' and the rest of his people, scarred as he was by the loss of his comrades, and he eventually took up the solitary life of a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]].<ref name="O66" />

With the True Mandalorians out of their way,<ref name="HotM" /> Death Watch finally moved against the New Mandalorians. During what became known as the Great Clan Wars,<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> the fragmented Death Watch<ref name="HotM" /> incited war against the New Mandalorian pacifists across Mandalore. The choice between standing with the New Mandalorians and supporting the Death Watch turned several clans against one another, and Mandalore suffered through a violent, second civil war that left fresh scars across the planet's surface and many dead. The tide of the war shifted with the entrance of [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]] into the conflict: Kryze, the daughter of [[Clan Kryze/Legends|her clan's]] preeminent [[Satine Kryze's father/Legends|chieftain]] turned staunch New Mandalorian pacifist, wielded her words and charisma in lieu of weapons, winning over several of the warring clan leaders to her peaceful cause. Death Watch and their goals were ultimately thwarted, as a number of defeated but unrepentant Mandalorian [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] accepted [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] to Mandalore's moon Concordia,<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> where the New Mandalorian government assumed and expected that they would die out.<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> Their strength renewed, the New Mandalorians appointed Satine Kryze as their new ''Mand'alor''—though she ruled the New Mandalorian faction<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> initially in opposition to Jango Fett, who possessed the title among the warrior clans until his death years later in the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]].<ref name="O66" /> As the new leader of the New Mandalorians, Kryze set about rebuilding the damage incurred to Mandalore during the war.<ref name="TCW:VoT" />

===The Clone Wars===
====Return of the Death Watch====
{{Quote|Mandalore is making great strides to find the leaders of this terrorist movement. They are not powerful enough to destabilize our government. We will resolve this without conflict.|Satine Kryze|<ref name="TCW:DoM" />}}
Duchess Satine Kryze continued to lead the New Mandalorians as the galaxy-spanning [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] broke out between the Galactic Republic and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] in 22 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]]. By that point in time, New Mandalorian territory<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> had prospered greatly<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> in the years following the end of the Great Clan Wars.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> Under Kryze's leadership, Mandalore was declared a neutral world at the Clone War's onset, with Kryze even elected to lead the [[Council of Neutral Systems/Legends|Council of Neutral Systems]],<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> a collective of other worlds and [[Star/Legends|star]] systems that wished to remain uninvolved in the conflict. But while the New Mandalorians had been making a steady recovery in the wake of the last bloody civil war,<ref name="TCW:VoT" /> so too had Death Watch. As ever, the resurgent Death Watch<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> despised the peace-loving government the New Mandalorians had established, viewing the administration as weak and Kryze as a disgrace to all Mandalorians for their pacifist views. They allied with [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], [[Head of State/Legends|leader]] of the Confederacy of Independent Systems, to gain the means necessary to remove Kryze and the New Mandalorians from power.<ref name="TCW:TMP" />

[[File:Memorial_Shrine_bombing.jpg|thumb|left|300px|As [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Duchess Kryze]] showed [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] around Sundari, the Death Watch [[Attack on the Memorial Shrine/Legends|bombed]] the [[Memorial Shrine/Legends|Memorial Shrine]]]]
An [[Attack on a Republic cruiser/Legends|attack]] on a [[Unidentified Republic cruiser|Republic cruiser]] by a [[Unidentified Death Watch saboteur/Legends|Death Watch]] [[Commando/Legends|commando]], along with circulating rumors that the New Mandalorians weren't as peaceful as they wanted the galaxy to believe, drew the attention of the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]], who dispatched [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]<ref name="TCW:TMP" />—an old friend and one-time lover of Satine Kryze<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" />—to Mandalore in order to investigate the current state of Mandalorian affairs.<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> Kenobi arrived at the New Mandalorian capital of Sundari,<ref name="TMPEpGuide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode212.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: The Mandalore Plot}}</ref> where he was [[Hover taxi/Legends|ferried]] from the city's [[Sundari shipping docks/Legends|docks]] to the Royal Palace in order to meet with Duchess Kryze. There, he was greeted by the New Mandalorians' Prime Minister [[Almec/Legends|Almec]], who assured Kenobi that the New Mandalorians were committed to peaceful coexistence with the Republic, disavowing any connection to Mandalore's warriors. Kryze arrived shortly thereafter, and invited the Jedi Master to accompany her on a walk through Sundari to display how far things had progressed<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> since the Great Clan Wars' end,<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> all the while assuring Kenobi that the New Mandalorians remained firmly dedicated to peace. Despite this, Kenobi discovered the threat posed by the Death Watch when the [[Memorial Shrine/Legends|Memorial Shrine]] was violently [[Attack on the Memorial Shrine/Legends|bombed]] as Kenobi and Kryze had been walking nearby<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> in [[Peace Park/Legends|Peace Park]].<ref name="TCW:TA EPGuide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode306.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: The Academy}}</ref> Spotting [[Death Watch bomber/Legends|the bomber]] among the panicked and injured crowd of New Mandalorians at the scene, Kenobi attempted to detain the [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]], but the bomber instead chose to commit suicide rather than allow himself to be taken into custody by Kenobi.<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> As the bomber spoke in the [[Concordian/Legends|Concordian]] language during his final moments of life,<ref name="TMPEpGuide" /> Kenobi decided to follow the potential clue back to Concordia, Mandalore's moon, with Kryze as his escort.<ref name="TCW:TMP" />

Once on Concordia, Kenobi's investigation took him to an old [[Concordian mines/Legends|''beskar'' mine]] believed by the New Mandalorian government to be abandoned.<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> There, he was captured and incapacitated by the Death Watch,<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> who were secretly using the derelict [[Mining/Legends|mines]] to manufacture weapons and armor,<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> only to later be rescued by Kryze. As Kryze and Kenobi made their escape from the mines, they were confronted by a contingent of Death Watch soldiers under the leadership of their most recent [[Commander/Legends|commander]], [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]], [[Governor/Legends|governor]] of Concordia<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> and [[Clan Vizsla/Legends|clan kinsmen]]<ref name="TCWCE" /> of Death Watch's founder, Tor Vizsla.<ref name="TEA" /> The younger Vizsla had previously been a public supporter of Kryze and the New Mandalorian regime,<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> but had worked in secret for years to rebuild the Death Watch in the wake of the Great Clan Wars,<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> establishing a hidden [[Death Watch hideout|base]] in the Concordian mines from which Death Watch could move against the pacifists Vizsla viewed as a disgrace to the Mandalorian name.<ref name="TCW:TMP" />

[[File:PreVizslaDeathWatch-TheMandalorePlot.jpg|thumb|right|300px|[[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]], leading the resurgent [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]]]]
Pre Vizsla challenged Master Kenobi to [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|single combat]], [[Fight on Concordia/Legends|engaging him]] with an ancient [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] of his own,<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> the [[Lightsaber crystal/Legends|black]]-bladed [[Darksaber/Legends|Darksaber]] that had been passed down through his clan.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> Despite his own skill with the blade, Vizsla was unable to best the Jedi Master in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|combat]] on his own, ordering his Death Watch subordinates to finish Kenobi with [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpack]]-launched [[Missile/Legends|missiles]]. The chaos of the resulting explosion allowed Kenobi and Kryze the opportunity to flee Concordia and return to Sundari.<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> Evidence of the significant threat Death Watch posed led to the Galactic Senate drafting a [[Mandalore Defense Resolution/Legends|defense initiative]] that would send a [[Garrison/Legends|garrison]] of the Republic's [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army]] to occupy Mandalore as a peacekeeping force. The New Mandalorian government was highly opposed to the idea, confident that they would be able to handle Death Watch on their own, and desiring Mandalore to maintain its neutral status instead of becoming a military target in the war due to a Republic [[Clone trooper/Legends|presence]]. Intent on pleading her government's case against the proposed occupation before the Galactic Senate,<ref name="TCW:DoM" /> Duchess Kryze traveled to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] aboard her personal [[Starship/Legends|starship]],<ref name="TCW:VoT" /> the grand [[Coronet/Legends|''Coronet'']] [[Passenger liner/Legends|starliner]],<ref name="TCWIV" /> with the New Mandalorian senator [[Tal Merrik/Legends|Tal Merrik]]<ref name="TCWCE" /> and a retinue of political sympathizers.<ref name="TCW:VoT" />

During the voyage to Coruscant, Senator Merrik proved himself a traitor to the New Mandalorian cause and a Death Watch ally when he [[Skirmish aboard the Coronet/Legends|attempted to have Kryze killed]] aboard the ''Coronet'', unleashing a band of [[Assassin probe/Legends|assassin probes]] from the vessel's cargo hold. The [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droids]] were foiled by Master Kenobi's continuing protection of Kryze, along with a small detachment of [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Troop/Legends|troopers]] under the command of [[Clone Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Rex/Legends|Rex]], [[Clone Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Cody/Legends|Cody]], and Kenobi's former [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]. His initial plan ruined, Merrik took Kryze hostage at [[Blaster/Legends|blasterpoint]], and called in [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droid]] reinforcements from Death Watch's Confederacy allies to deal with the clones and Jedi. Though he attempted to flee the ''Coronet'' with the captive duchess, Merrik initiated a contingency plan wherein he could detonate the ship's [[Engine/Legends|engines]] with a hand-held [[Detonator/Legends|detonator]], killing everyone aboard including himself, if his escape could not be secured. Amid a standoff between Obi-Wan Kenobi and Merrik, it was Kenobi's former Padawan Skywalker who brought an end to the threat Merrick posed by [[Shiak|killing]] the New Mandalorian senator and securing the detonator.<ref name="TCW:VoT" />

[[File:KryzeJerecTestimony-DuchessOfMandalore.png|thumb|left|275px|Satine Kryze speaks out against the Republic's [[Mandalore Defense Resolution/Legends|plans]] to occupy Mandalore before the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]]]
Once safely on Coruscant, Duchess Kryze went before an assembly of the Republic senate, hoping to convince the gathered senators that an intrusion by the Republic into Mandalorian affairs would only make the situation worse,<ref name="TCW:DoM" /> and a Republic occupation would incite the population of Mandalore to violent rebellion.<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> However, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] presented [[Hologram/Legends|recorded]] testimony from the New Mandalorians' Deputy Minister [[Jerec/Legends|Jerec]], in which the statesman indicated that it was their government's pride that brought Kryze before the Galactic Senate and that if they were to have any success in stopping the Death Watch, the New Mandalorians would need Republic assistance. Unknown to nearly all involved, the evidence had been [[Holo faker|doctored]] from Jerec's original statement; Kryze's existing relationship with the Deputy Minister made her question the validity of his apparent testimony, but when she demanded to speak with him, Chancellor Palpatine informed the Duchess that Jerec had been killed in a Death Watch [[Bombing on Kalevala/Legends|bombing on Kalevala]] the [[Standard day/Legends|day]] prior. On that solemn note, the senatorial session was adjourned and the vote on the resolution was scheduled for the following day. Duchess Kryze left the [[Senate Building/Legends|Senate Building]], only to [[Plot to assassinate Satine Kryze/Legends|come under attack]] from a [[Unidentified Death Watch assassin/Legends|Death Watch assassin]] sent to Coruscant with orders to terminate her life by Pre Vizsla. Her [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]] was destroyed and [[Aramis/Legends|her pilot]] killed, but Kryze managed to escape the ordeal physically unharmed. As an unexpected result of the attack, the Senate decided that the Death Watch threat required more immediate action, and elected to move up the vote, passing a resolution that would see Republic troops departing for Mandalore the following morning.<ref name="TCW:DoM" />

At the same time, Prime Minister Almec had dispatched a [[Unidentified New Mandalorian scout/Legends|New Mandalorian scout]] to Concordia, who was able to ascertain that the Death Watch was indeed assembling an [[Army/Legends|army]] in preparation for the Republic's arrival.<ref name="TCW:DoM" /> A shrewd [[Politics/Legends|politician]],<ref name="TCWCE" /> Almec was able to correctly deduce the Death Watch's plan from the [[Scout/Legends|scout's]] report: instigating a conflict with the Republic, the Death Watch would gain the populace's support by appearing to be liberators against an oppressive off-world occupation<ref name="TCW:DoM" /> the likes of which Mandalore had not endured since the end of the Mandalorian Excision.<ref name="TEGW" /> Even with this knowledge, however, there was little he could do on his own, and instead he put his faith in Kryze's ability to convince the Senate to see reason.<ref name="TCW:DoM" />

[[File:DeathWatchAbandonsConcordiaBase-DoM.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Due to Kryze's actions, Death Watch is forced to stand down and abandon their [[Death Watch hideout|base]] on [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]]]]
On Coruscant, Kryze met with [[Davu Golec/Legends|Davu Golec]] from the [[Republic Ministry of Intelligence/Legends|Republic Ministry of Intelligence]]. A supporter of Kryze and the New Mandalorian government, Golec had discovered that Jerec's presented testimony had been falsified, and turned over the original recording to Kryze before being [[Blaster/Legends|gunned]] down by the Death Watch assassin still targeting the Duchess. A misunderstanding at the scene of the crime on the part of the [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Force]] led to the belief that Kryze had been responsible for Golec's death, and she was forced to flee when CSF attempted to take her into custody. Kryze contacted Obi-Wan Kenobi for assistance while on the run, and together they passed along the true recording to Senator [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] so that she could present the findings to the senate. In light of the newfound evidence, the Senate ordered an emergency session, during which the earlier approval of the resolution was overturned and the Republic intervention force was decommissioned. Kryze was also cleared of all wrong-doing when it was discovered that Death Watch was responsible for Davu Golec's death. Although the Death Watch's plan had been foiled, Pre Vizsla contemplated attacking the New Mandalorians with his assembled army regardless, but was persuaded against such action by [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] Dooku; Dooku reasoned that without the backing of the Mandalorian people, any attempt to claim power by force would be met with failure,<ref name="TCW:DoM" /> just as they had for the previous incarnations of Death Watch<ref name="HotM" /> during the last wars.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> Due to Kryze's victory in the Galactic Senate,<ref name="TCW:DoM" /> Mandalore was allowed to uphold its neutral status and remain out of the Clone Wars.<ref name="Corruption" /> Defeated, Death Watch was later driven from the [[Mandalore system/Legends|Mandalore system]],<ref name="Zanbar">{{SWE|locations|zanbar|Zanbar}}</ref> becoming a nomadic band of Mandalorian outlaws wandering the galaxy.<ref name="DeathWatch">{{SWE|groups|deathwatch|Death Watch}}</ref>

====Corruption and conspiracy====
{{Quote|I'm afraid our neutrality has caused our people to suffer. The war between the Separatists and the Republic rages across our galaxy. This caused trade routes to be closed to Mandalore, and has forced us to turn to a black market filled with corruption.|Almec, speaking before the New Mandalorian [[Ruling Council (New Mandalorians)/Legends|Ruling Council]]|<ref name="Corruption" />}}
Despite the successes of Duchess Satine Kryze in allowing Mandalore to remain out of the galactic war, peace came at a price for the New Mandalorians. With their declaration that Mandalore would remain a neutral entity, much of the Republic's hierarchy viewed the New Mandalorians now on the outside of Republic concerns; Republic trade routes to Mandalore were largely shut down and re-prioritized elsewhere.<ref name="Corruption" /> Having isolated themselves<ref name="TEA" /> from Mandalore's [[Farm/Legends|farming]] communities in the verdant parts of Mandalore<ref name="O66" /> left unscathed by the Mandalorian Excision,<ref name="TEGW" /> the New Mandalorians began to suffer from food shortages without Republic aid, leaving many of the faction's citizens starving.<ref name="Corruption" /> In an effort to remedy the situation, Prime Minister Almec took it upon himself to [[Mandalorian black market conspiracy/Legends|establish]] a [[Black market/Legends|black market]] trade network in secret, going against the wishes of Duchess Kryze in order to get the supplies the New Mandalorian people so desperately needed.<ref name="SoR" />

[[File:SickNewMandoKids.png|thumb|left|300px|Sick from [[Slabin/Legends|tainted]] [[Ardees Beverage/Legends|tea]] imports, New Mandalorian children flocked to [[Sundari Mandalorian hospital/Legends|Sundari hospitals]] seeking medical treatment]]
The illegal intake of supplies to Sundari came at a dangerous cost: [[Moogan/Legends|Moogan]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]]<ref name="CorruptionEpGuide" /> arrived in Sundari, [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|bribing]] their way passed [[Unidentified Mandalorian customs official/Legends|customs officials]] in order to unload shipments of [[Ardees Beverage/Legends|Ardees Beverage tea]]. Looking to increase their total profits from the shipment, the Moogans diluted the [[Tea/Legends|tea]] with [[Slabin/Legends|slabin]] from a [[Sundari dock warehouse/Legends|warehouse]] at Sundari's docks, but instead of a harmless mixture, the slabin dosage was incorrectly calculated, contaminating the tea. The tea was distributed to a number of New Mandalorian [[school]]s, resulting in hundreds of children becoming violently ill, many of whom were taken to a recently opened [[Sundari Mandalorian hospital/Legends|hospital]] in Sundari. The hospital was set to be toured that day by Duchess Kryze and her offworld guest, Senator Padmé Amidala—visiting Sundari to discuss the reinstitution of Republic aid to the New Mandalorian people—and upon discovering the outbreak of [[Poison/Legends|poisoned]] youths, Kryze and Amidala set out to discover the source of the illness plaguing the New Mandalorians sect's schoolchildren. Upon visiting [[Sundari Mandalorian school/Legends|one school]] that had been affected, the two politicians discovered the [[Ardees Beverage Company/Legends|Ardees]] bottled tea to be the source of the poison, and traced the shipment back to the Sundari warehouse out of which the Moogan smugglers were operating. Following a [[Skirmish at the Sundari docks/Legends|brief shootout]] between the smugglers and several members of the Mandalorian Royal Guard, the operation was dismantled and an antidote was provided to the hospitalized children,<ref name="Corruption" /> though many New Mandalorian children had already succumbed to the contaminated drinks and died as a result.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> Prime Minister Almec was confronted by Kryze at the conclusion of her investigation—though she did not yet know of his involvement—and in an effort to ease her concerns, he assured the Duchess that he intended to form a committee to look into the corruption lurking amongst the New Mandalorians' officials, but this did little to quell Kryze's misgivings. Instead, the Duchess requested a member of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] come to Mandalore in order to help stop the black market trade network, and lecture against the perils of corruption at the Royal Academy of Government.<ref name="Corruption" /> Agreeing to the request, the Jedi Council dispatched Jedi Padawan [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] to Mandalore.<ref name="TCW:TA" />

[[File:MandoBlackMarket-TA.png|thumb|right|280px|A cloaked [[Almec/Legends|Almec]] secretly meeting with a group of [[Gotal/Legends|Gotal]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]]]]
Arriving in Sundari, Tano lectured for days at Sundari's Royal Academy, speaking on the subject of corruption among government leadership, and the duty of the common citizen to ensure lawful behavior among society's rulers. Taking the Jedi's words to [[Heart/Legends|heart]], a group of New Mandalorian [[Cadet/Legends|cadets]] aware of the city's food shortages—[[Amis/Legends|Amis]], [[Lagos/Legends|Lagos]], [[Soniee/Legends|Soniee]], and Duchess Kryze's own nephew, [[Korkie Kryze/Legends|Korkie]]—decided to investigate Sundari's [[Sundari warehouse district/Legends|warehouse district]] for any signs of misconduct. Infiltrating the facility, the four New Mandalorian youths discovered a [[Government warehouse/Legends|government warehouse]] being used to store black market goods, and a secret meeting between a group of New Mandalorian officers, several [[Gotal/Legends|Gotal]] smugglers, and an unknown being draped in a concealing cloak. They informed Duchess Kryze of the meeting they had witnessed, only to be met with a warning of caution. Instead, the cadets turn to Prime Minister Almec with their find, unaware that he was in fact the cloaked man from the warehouse. Fearing the repercussions of his discovery, Almec moved against the cadets and had them arrested by the [[Mandalorian secret service/Legends|New Mandalorian Secret Service]], along with their Jedi ally Padawan Tano, and even the Duchess herself. He attempted to have the Duchess sign a confession of conspiracy, incriminating herself as the one responsible for the black market network, going so far as to use a [[Shock collar/Legends|shock collar]] as a means of [[Torture/Legends|persuading]] her. Kryze would not yield, and soon after, Tano and the cadets fought back, managing to overpower Almec and his guards until he could be fitted with a shock collar himself, forcing the Prime Minister to surrender. Almec and his conspirators were placed under arrest and subsequently [[Prison/Legends|imprisoned]],<ref name="TCW:TA" /> having been found guilty on charges of corruption by Sundari's courts. Almec was replaced as Prime Minister of the New Mandalorians by [[Armatan/Legends|Armatan]],<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> the former New Mandalorian Minister of the Interior,<ref name="CorruptionEpGuide" /> while the black market trade network was left in ruins.<ref name="TCW:TA" />

====The Death Watch coup====
{{Quote|Listen, Duchess. Do you hear the people? They cry out for change. Your weak-minded rule of Mandalore is at an end. The resurrection of our warrior past is about to begin!|Pre Vizsla, speaking to Satine Kryze|<ref name="SoR" />}}
[[File:Moj-TakeoverOnMandalore.png|thumb|left|280px|The New Mandalorians come [[Takeover of Mandalore/Legends|under attack]] from the [[Shadow Collective/Legends|Shadow Collective's]] foot soldiers]]
Two years since Death Watch had last attempted to remove the New Mandalorians from power, Sundari and other New Mandalorian holdings across Mandalore came under attack by a contingent of offworld [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]] known as the [[Shadow Collective/Legends|Shadow Collective]]. Comprised of elements of [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]], the [[Spice/Legends|spice]]-[[Drug dealer|dealing]] [[Pyke Syndicate/Legends|Pyke Syndicate]] of Coruscant, and the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartels]], these gangsters were secretly in collusion with the Death Watch after Pre Vizsla forged an alliance with their leader, the rogue [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], to topple the New Mandalorians' pacifist regime. As part of a plan to exemplify the ineffectiveness of the New Mandalorian administration, the Collective's thugs rampaged throughout Sundari, overwhelming a police force that proved incapable of defending against the aggressors. The capital city's docks fell quickly into Collective control, while [[Pyke/Legends|Pyke]] gangsters assaulted the<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> [[Mandalore Banking Center/Legends|Mandalore Banking Center]],<ref name="SoREpGuide">{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep515|text="Shades of Reason" - ''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide|nolive=1}}</ref> and [[Black Sun foot soldier/Legends|Black Sun foot soldiers]] opened fire on Peace Park with reckless abandon, killing civilian and [[Police officer/Legends|police officers]] alike.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> Panicked, dense crowds of New Mandalorians gathered at the Sundari Royal Palace to demand action from their leaders, only to be advised to remain calm and cautioned to keep to their peaceful principles by Duchess Satine Kryze. It was then that Death Watch made their presence known, as Pre Vizsla publicly pledged to do what Kryze could not: defend the New Mandalorians against the crime syndicates and keep Sundari safe.<ref name="SoR" />

At the docks of Sundari, Death Watch troops subdued the Black Sun and Pyke forces holding the dock workers captive, freeing the grateful New Mandalorians and taking the criminals into custody.<ref name="SoR" /> In Peace Park, Pre Vizsla's loyal [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] [[Bo-Katan Kryze/Legends|Bo-Katan]] and her handpicked [[Squad/Legends|unit]] known as the [[Nite Owls/Legends|Nite Owls]]<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> rescued a number of New Mandalorian children from Black Sun footsoldiers, [[Whipcord launcher/Legends|binding]] the gangsters with [[Fibercord/Legends|fibercord]], while Vizsla himself apprehended a team of Pyke thugs led by [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Maul's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]], [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]], as they attempted to flee the pilfered<ref name="SoR" /> Mandalore [[Bank/Legends|Banking]] Center.<ref name="SoREpGuide" /> The Collective had played the role of villains to be vanquished by the Death Watch well,<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> and as the Mandalorian warriors triumphed over the offworld gangsters, the New Mandalorian populous applauded their efforts and lauded the Death Watch as saviors. With the fervent support of the New Mandalorian people, Pre Vizsla marched on the Royal Palace with a cadre of Death Watch soldiers, deposing and [[Prisoner/Legends|imprisoning]] Duchess Kryze and her supporters, going so far as to kill those officials who refused to side with him. Vizsla declared himself the new Prime Minister,<ref name="SoR" /> replacing Armatan, while claiming the title of ''Mand'alor'' of the New Mandalorians.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" />

[[File:AlmecDeathWatch-ShadesOfReason.png|thumb|right|300px|The reinstituted [[Prime Minister/Legends|Prime Minister]] Almec addresses the New Mandalorian people, flanked by Death Watch soldiers]]
His ambitions met, Vizsla turned on his [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] allies and had both [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Maul and his apprentice, Savage Opress, jailed. However, the two Sith [[Telekinesis/Legends|broke free]] of their confines shortly after, and came across the captive former Prime Minister Almec within the [[Royal prison/Legends|Sundari prison]] complex; deciding the deposed politician would make a suitable, more malleable replacement for Vizsla, Maul and Opress broke free of the prison with Almec in tow, storming the Royal Palace. There, Maul challenged Vizsla to a duel for leadership, and despite a furious show of skill and force from Vizsla, Maul emerged triumphant, [[Sai cha/Legends|beheading]] Vizsla and claiming the right to succeed him as leader of Death Watch. While Vizsla's lieutenant Bo-Katan and a squad of other Death Watch soldiers refused to kneel to a non-Mandalorian, fleeing the palace amidst a hail of [[Lightfight|blasterfire]], many of Vizsla's former troops bowed to the victorious Sith [[Lord/Legends|Lord]]<ref name="SoR" /> and accepted Maul<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> as their new [[Secret Mandalore]].<ref name="TBHC" /> By Maul's new authority, Almec was reinstituted as Prime Minister of the New Mandalorians, serving as a public face and puppet ruler behind which Maul could reign in secret, his presence unknown to the people of Mandalore beyond the ranks of Death Watch. With his position returned, Almec spoke before a gathering of the New Mandalorian people, detailing a story in which Duchess Kryze had been responsible for Vizsla's murder and that it had been Vizsla's last wish for Almec to return to office as Prime Minister in order to attend to the plights of the populous in his absence. Stating that it was in accordance with Vizsla's last wishes, Almec also assuring the New Mandalorians that Vizsla's goals of remilitarization would live on.<ref name="SoR" />

Further [[Battle of Mandalore/Legends|conflict]] broke out when Bo-Katan and the Death Watch troops that had turned their backs on Darth Maul attempted to free Duchess Kryze from her confines and flee the city. Though they were successful in reaching Sundari's outer docks, Maul's loyal<ref name="Lawless">{{TCW|The Lawless}}</ref> [[Mandalorian super commando/Legends|Mandalorian super commandos]]<ref name="SuperCommandos">{{SWE|groups|mandalorian-super-commando|Mandalorian super commando}}</ref> overtook and recaptured Kryze before she could do anything more than send a request for aid to Obi-Wan Kenobi at the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on Coruscant. Knowing the Republic would be unable to send official aid to deal with the Death Watch threat due to Mandalore's neutrality, Kenobi journeyed<ref name="Lawless" /> to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] world<ref name="TEA" /> alone and in disguise, sneaking into Sundari in order to free his former lover. This rescue attempt was as doomed to failure as the first, as Kenobi's [[Twilight/Legends|starship]] was destroyed and he was apprehended along with Kryze by a vengeful Darth Maul. Taken back to the palace, Maul killed Kryze before Kenobi's [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]<ref name="Lawless" /> in recompense for the grievous injuries the Jedi Master had [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|inflicted]] upon him more than a decade prior.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> Rather than kill Kenobi outright, Maul instead chose to have him thrown into prison to live with the grief of Kryze's death, but before Kenobi could ever reach his intended jail cell, he was rescued by Bo-Katan and her faction of Death Watch. Bo-Katan rushed the Jedi Master out of Sundari and off of Mandalore amid a heated battle between her Death Watch soldiers and their former comrades that were now loyal to Darth Maul. Concurrent to Kenobi's escape was the arrival of Darth Sidious, who had [[Force sense/Legends|sensed]] the whereabouts of his one-time apprentice Darth Maul, and traveled to Mandalore in order to confront him over a breach of the [[Order of the Sith Lords|Sith Order's]] [[Rule of Two/Legends|Rule of Two]]. In Sundari's Royal Palace, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] faced off against Maul and Savage Opress, in a lightsaber duel that saw the death of the Opress and the subjugation of Maul at Sidious's [[Limb/Legends|hands]], though Maul was spared in order to serve the Dark Lord's own future purposes.<ref name="Lawless" />

===Decline===
{{Quote|However, from this point on, Mandalore ''will'' be strong, and we ''will'' be known as the warriors we were always meant to be!|Almec, reinstated Prime Minister of the New Mandalorians, addressing his people|<ref name="SoR" />}}
[[File:MandalorianProtectors-GAW.jpg|thumb|left|220px|The [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]]]]
Backed by the criminal forces of the Shadow Collective, the Death Watch's coup<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> proved to be too much for the New Mandalorians. Their government fell in the face of Death Watch's rise,<ref name="SW:TLJ">[[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']]</ref> while the Mandalorian revanchists eventually put an end to the New Mandalorians as a faction.<ref name="TEA" />

Mandalore's position in the Clone Wars changed with the arrival of [[Spar]] on Mandalore. The former Republic [[Alpha-class Advanced Recon Commando|ARC trooper]], previously known as Alpha-Ø2, deserted the Grand Army and fled from [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] before the start of the Clone Wars. Traveling the galaxy as a mercenary, he came to Mandalore following the death of Jango Fett on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], and there he met a local [[Constable/Legends|constable]]<ref name="HotM" /> and clan chieftain by the name of [[Fenn Shysa]]. Shysa, who saw Jango Fett as a symbol of strength for Mandalore, persuaded the clone to act as Fett's heir<ref name="O66" /> and take up the vacant role of ''Mand'alor''. Spar did, becoming "Mandalore the Resurrector," and forging a new army of supercommandos in the image of the fallen True Mandalorians<ref name="GaW">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref> which he dubbed the [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]].<ref name="HotM" /> Spar won out over the broken New Mandalorians,<ref name="TEA" /> and overturned the New Mandalorians' position of neutrality,<ref name="Lawless" /> instead allying Mandalore with the Confederacy of Independent Systems in order to oppose a Republic he viewed as oppressive and the Jedi Order, whom he blamed for their part in destroying the True Mandalorians<ref name="HotM" /> and their willingness to lead the Grand Army's [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone soldiers]].<ref name="O66" /> The New Mandalorians would never manage to reclaim their lost dominance, and under Spar, the warrior clans and Jaster Mereel's Supercommando Codex returned to the forefront of Mandalorian culture on Mandalore.<ref name="TEA" />

==Notable New Mandalorians==
===Satine Kryze===
{{Main|Satine Kryze/Legends}}
[[File:SatineKryze-Corruption.png|thumb|right|225px|Duchess Satine Kryze, the New Mandalorian leader and icon of their beliefs]]
{{Quote|The Duchess Satine values peace more than her own life.|Almec|<ref name="TCW:TMP" />}}
The daughter of the chieftain of Clan Kryze,<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> Satine Kryze hailed from the planet Kalevala.<ref name="TCW:VoT" /> During the Great Clan Wars, as the Death Watch attempted to overthrow the New Mandalorian regime in a bloody civil war, Kryze's father sent her away to Coruscant in order to gain an education in [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomacy]] and statecraft, and be free of the violence that would eventually claim the clan leader's life. When Kryze returned to the Mandalore system, she did so under the protection of Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his Padawan Obi-Wan Kenobi; for [[Standard month/Legends|months]], Kryze was under constant threat from the Death Watch and its allies, but as time went on, Kryze was able to use the skills she had learned and her own charisma to rally war-weary chieftains to the New Mandalorian cause and bring about peace. Following the end of the Great Clan Wars, Kryze was appointed ''Mand'alor'' by the New Mandalorian people, and as ''Mand'alor'',<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> she set about rebuilding the damage incurred to Mandalore<ref name="TCW:VoT" /> during the Great Clan Wars, leading New Mandalorian society and its capital city Sundari<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> to prosperity.<ref name="TCW:TMP" />

Upon the outbreak of the Clone Wars, Kryze strove to ensure Mandalore would remain neutral in the conflict, though the peace she had made came under siege by the re-emergence of the Death Watch.<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> Though Kryze was able to overcome their initial schemes and attempts on her life<ref name="TCW:DoM" /> to solidify Mandalore's neutrality, as the Clone Wars went on, her rule was marred with severe food shortages, a rise in New Mandalorian corruption, and mass poisonings throughout New Mandalorian territory as a result of toxin-laced tea imported by Moogan smugglers.<ref name="Corruption" /> In 20 BBY, Death Watch allied with the Shadow Collective to bring down the New Mandalorians: public opinion swayed against Kryze as offworld gangsters mercilessly gunned down civilians and caused panic, only for the Death Watch to arrive and act as saviors of the people, defeating and arresting their secret allies in a show of apparent heroism. With the support of her people gone, Kryze was deposed and imprisoned, replaced as ''Mand'alor'' by Death Watch leader Pre Vizsla. Weeks later, when her old friend Obi-Wan Kenobi came to Mandalore in order to rescue Kryze from prison, she was murdered in front of the Jedi Master by the Sith Lord Darth Maul, who had been in collusion with Vizsla during his coup and sought to pain Kenobi with his one-time lover's death.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> Despite her achievements,<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> Kryze's legitimacy as ''Mand'alor'' was not recognized by the Mandalorian warrior clans in the years that followed,<ref name="O66" /> and the New Mandalorian faction was eventually destroyed.<ref name="TEA" />

===Almec===
{{Main|Almec/Legends}}
[[File:Almec_SWE.png|thumb|right|170px|Almec, twice appointed Prime Minister of the New Mandalorians]]
{{Quote|What you did for the people as Prime Minister betrayed their trust.''"<br />"''And you betrayed mine. Destitution leaves little room for faith. My actions allowed the people hope in your leadership. The supplies I bought on the black market kept you in power.''"<br />"''Another error of judgement.|Satine Kryze and Almec|<ref name="SoR" />}}
A Mandalore native,<ref name="TCWCE" /> Almec grew up a member of the New Mandalorian faction. He despised the traditional Mandalorian warrior ways,<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> and took great pride in the success the New Mandalorian government had in renouncing the violent reputation Mandalore had held in the past. He came to resent the opinion of offworlders who associated Mandalore only with the planet's warrior clans rather than the progressive New Mandalorian society, and was a strong believer in the sect's pacifist beliefs.<ref name="TCWCE" /> Almec was named Prime Minister of the New Mandalorian people by the start of the Clone Wars,<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> but despite his high-ranking office<ref name="Corruption" /> and talents as a diplomat, Almec was a humble man, who preferred simple clothes<ref name="TCWCE" /> and considered himself a servant of the people.<ref name="TCW:TMP" />

However, it was his dedication to the New Mandalorian people that would be his downfall:<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> the black market trade network that Almec took it upon himself to establish<ref name="TCW:TA" /> during lean times in New Mandalorian society led to Moogan smugglers importing tainted tea that poisoned<ref name="Corruption" /> and killed New Mandalorian children. When his complicity in these deaths were discovered, Almec was imprisoned on charges of corruption. Two years later, Almec rode out a Death Watch coup against the New Mandalorians in the safety of his cell in a Sundari prison. But when he was approached by the rogue Sith Lord Darth Maul with the promise of power, Almec was freed of captivity and returned to his former position as Prime Minister. With Death Watch and Maul in power now, Almec renounced his former pacifism in the belief that war would again be the future of Mandalore, and agreed to loyally serve Darth Maul as a puppet ruler of the New Mandalorians.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|For the inspiration of the civilization, I gave them kind of a very Nordic kind of flavor, looking at a civilization and the struggle that exists between the pacifism that Satine is trying to implement, and the, you know, terror and barbarism that Pre Vizsla wants to bring back.|[[Dave Filoni]]|<ref name="CMF" />}}
The New Mandalorians first entered into ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] via a mention in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', a [[2009]] reference guide [[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Jason Fry]],<ref name="TEA" /> before making their visual debut in the [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]] of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series, appearing in a trilogy of episodes comprised of "[[The Mandalore Plot]],"<ref name="TCW:TMP" /> "[[Voyage of Temptation]],"<ref name="TCW:VoT" /> and "[[Duchess of Mandalore]]."<ref name="TCW:DoM" /> Following their initial introduction, the New Mandalorians would continue to be a reoccurring presence in the television series, reappearing later in the second season's "[[Senate Murders]],",<ref name="SenateMurders">{{TCW|Senate Murders}}</ref> and in the [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|third season]] episodes "[[Corruption (episode)|Corruption]],"<ref name="Corruption" /> "[[The Academy]],"<ref name="TCW:TA" /> and "[[Pursuit of Peace]]."<ref name="PoP">{{TCW|Pursuit of Peace}}</ref> During ''The Clone Wars'' series' [[The Clone Wars: Season Four|fourth season]], several New Mandalorians appeared in minor roles in the episodes "[[A Friend in Need]]"<ref name="TCW:AFiN">{{TCW|A Friend in Need}}</ref> and "[[Deception]]."<ref name="TCW:Deception">{{TCW|Deception}}</ref> The release of the young reader novel ''[[The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy]]'' by Jason Fry,<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /> along with three of the television series [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|fifth season]] episodes the novel adapted—"[[Eminence (episode)|Eminence]],"<ref name="Eminence" /> "[[Shades of Reason]],"<ref name="SoR" /> and "[[The Lawless]]"<ref name="Lawless" />—saw the downfall of the New Mandalorians, brought on by a Death Watch coup with the aid of Darth Maul.<ref name="TCW:DM:SC" />

The New Mandalorians were introduced to ''The Clone Wars'' television series in a way that differed significantly from the manner in which Mandalorians had been more commonly portrayed in the ''Star Wars'' [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] prior to that point in time:<ref name="CMF" /> the New Mandalorians adhered to pacifistic neutrality and non-violence,<ref name="TEA" /> in a culture otherwise established as one of clan-based soldiers and mercenaries.<ref name="HotM" /><ref name="TMPaC" /> Although the choice to portray a group of Mandalorians in this way was a radical departure of what had come before,<ref name="CMF" /> the New Mandalorians' commitment to peace was an essential aspect of their overarching narrative throughout the television series.<ref name="TCW:TMP" /><ref name="TCW:DM:SC" /><ref name="TCW:DoM" /> Discrepancies between the portrayals of the two societies, one of pacifist desert-dwellers and one of soldierly ruralists, were reconciled through a variety of reference books including ''The Essential Atlas''<ref name="TEA" /> and ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: New Battlefronts: The Visual Guide]]'',<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> while ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' detailed additional aspects of the New Mandalorians' in-universe foundation and rise.<ref name="TEGW" />
